detail: Page date: Apr 1, 2026 | quote: "Apr 1, 2026"
Linear refresh failures commonly return HTTP 400 with OAuth error `invalid_grant`. | quote: "Common HTTP status: 400

The error means the stored refresh token cannot mint a new access token, and retrying the same request will continue failing. | quote: "the refresh token you have stored can’t be used to mint a new access token. Retrying the same request will keep failing"

Root causes include invalid, expired, revoked, or stale refresh tokens after rotation. | quote: "This happens because the token is invalid, expired, revoked, or you’re using a stale token after rotation."

Linear rotates refresh tokens; exchanging one invalidates the previous access and refresh tokens. | quote: "when a refresh token is exchanged, the previous access and refresh tokens are invalidated and new tokens are returned."

Concurrent refreshes can cause one process to overwrite the current refresh token with a stale one. | quote: "one process stores the “new” refresh token, another process overwrites it with the stale one, and suddenly every refresh starts failing."
Linear access tokens expire in 24 hours when refresh tokens are enabled. | quote: "Linear access tokens expire in 24 hours when refresh tokens are enabled."

An inactive, expired refresh token causes `invalid_grant` and requires re-authorization. | quote: "if the refresh token itself has expired due to inactivity, Linear returns invalid_grant and requires re-authorization."
Removing or revoking the app invalidates all associated tokens. | quote: "Linear immediately invalidates all associated tokens."

Refresh requests may be rejected because the token was already rotated, retried after a duplicate-refresh grace period, or sent with incorrect client credentials. | quote: "The refresh token is stale because it was already rotated"
Scope or app-configuration changes can invalidate existing refresh tokens and require re-authorization. | quote: "existing refresh tokens may become invalid and require re-authorization."

Incorrect client credentials can result from secret rotation, wrong workspace credentials, or environment-variable errors. | quote: "Using incorrect client_id or client_secret when refreshing tokens will result in invalid_grant errors."
Simultaneous refreshes by multiple workers create a race in which a worker uses a stale token. | quote: "Worker B refreshes with the now-stale token and gets invalid_grant"

Security heuristics may revoke tokens for unusual access patterns, suspicious activity, rate-limit violations, or detected compromise. | quote: "Linear may revoke refresh tokens based on security heuristics or policy changes."

Persist every new `refresh_token` returned by Linear and use it for the next refresh. | quote: "If Linear returns a new refresh_token on refresh, always persist it and use that value for the next refresh."
Refresh requests should use `grant_type=refresh_token`, form encoding, appropriate client authentication, and Linear’s token endpoint. | quote: "grant_type=refresh_token

detail: The Notion API enforces both per-connection and per-workspace rate limits. | quote: "The Notion API enforces two rate limits: a per-connection limit and a per-workspace limit. Some endpoints also have their own limit."

Each connection’s request budget is calculated over a 60-second window according to the workspace plan. | quote: "Each connection has a fixed budget of requests per 60-second window, based on the workspace’s plan:"

Business and Enterprise workspaces have a per-connection limit of 600 requests per minute, averaging 10 requests per second. | quote: "Business and Enterprise 600 requests per minute (an average of 10 per second)"
All other plans have a per-connection limit of 180 requests per minute, averaging 3 requests per second. | quote: "All other plans 180 requests per minute (an average of 3 per second)"

The per-connection budget may be used evenly or in a single burst within the 60-second window. | quote: "The budget can be spent at any pace within the window — spread out evenly or in a single burst."

When the per-connection limit is exceeded, Retry-After indicates the time until the window resets and is at most 60 seconds. | quote: "When a request exceeds this limit, the Retry-After value is the time until the window resets, so it is at most 60 seconds."

Data-source queries have a separate limit of about 3 requests per second per connection and return HTTP 429 with Retry-After when exceeded. | quote: "Querying a data source has a separate limit of about 3 requests per second per connection. A request over this limit returns an HTTP 429 response with a Retry-After header."

A separate per-workspace limit is shared across all connections and can cause throttling even when each connection is within its own limit. | quote: "Because it’s shared, requests can be rate limited even when each individual connection is within its per-connection limit."
Retry-After for the shared workspace limit may exceed one minute. | quote: "Retry-After for this limit can be longer than a minute."
Requests exceeding a rate limit return the rate_limited error code and HTTP 429. | quote: "Requests that exceed a limit return a \"rate_limited\" error code and an HTTP 429 response."
The rate_limit_reason field identifies which rate limit was exceeded. | quote: "additional_data.rate_limit_reason says which limit was exceeded:"

A per-connection limit violation is identified by public_api_request_rate_limit; clients should wait for Retry-After. | quote: "public_api_request_rate_limit This connection is sending requests too fast. Wait for Retry-After ."

A shared workspace-budget violation is identified by public_api_space_request_rate_limit; clients should wait for Retry-After. | quote: "public_api_space_request_rate_limit The workspace’s shared budget is used up. Wait for Retry-After ."

Endpoint-specific throttling is identified by public_api_endpoint_rate_limit; clients should wait for Retry-After. | quote: "public_api_endpoint_rate_limit This endpoint has its own limit. Wait for Retry-After ."

Connections should handle both HTTP 429 and 529 responses and respect the Retry-After header. | quote: "Connections should handle HTTP 429 and 529 responses and respect the Retry-After response header."

Retry-After is an integer number of seconds, and clients should use its returned value rather than a fixed delay. | quote: "The header value is an integer number of seconds. Use the returned value rather than assuming a fixed wait."

A 529 response means Notion is temporarily overloaded and should be retried like a 429. | quote: "A 529 response carries the \"service_overload\" code and means Notion is temporarily overloaded; retry it the same way as a 429."

When Retry-After is present, the response body also provides the wait duration in additional_data.retry_after. | quote: "the body repeats the wait as additional_data.retry_after , a string of whole seconds"

For 429 or 529 responses, pause new requests for at least Retry-After seconds, retry the failed request, and use exponential backoff with jitter for subsequent failures. | quote: "If another 429 or 529 arrives, increase the delay with exponential backoff and jitter."

A 429 with public_api_request_blocked should not be retried because the connection’s API access is restricted. | quote: "Do not retry every error. Retry 429 and 529 responses, except a 429 with public_api_request_blocked ."

steps.title: Draft OAuth callback logic

detail.text: For a web-based agent, use a backend confidential OAuth client. Keep the client secret on the backend and never send it from a browser. Generate a random state for each connection, store it server-side with the user and an expiry, and validate it when Zoom redirects back. Exchange the authorization code from the backend, then atomically replace the stored refresh token. Use PKCE only for a native or other public client that has no backend server.

sources.quote: Zoom returns the same state value on the redirect, so your app can confirm that the response matches its request and prevent cross-site request forgery
A browser call exposes your client secret and fails with a CORS error.
